A QUICK FIELD GUIDE

Find your way through the universe.

01

Start with a complete experiment

Scenes loads a curated combination of objects, lighting, and viewpoints. Every scene can be edited.

02

Build the world

Elements lists every field, body, and background layer. Select any name to open its properties immediately; its switch shows or hides it. Display contains the spectrum, lensing, exposure, grid, and render quality. The shared Grid switch controls every field together.

03

Place an object, then get close

Elements → Add an object places individual bodies. Select it in Elements to edit its physical size and placement. Near a black hole, edit the orbit’s radius, height, and phase; in open space, use local positions in meters. Craft keep their true dimensions, so choose Track to see a tiny object up close.

Track follows a close-up camera around that body. Ride · 360° looks out from it; the NASA Shuttle uses its flight deck. Use Camera → Previous view to return, or Reset scene view to restore the scene’s starting viewpoint.

Enterprise systems: select the Enterprise in Elements to switch its warp drive on or off and shape its field. Bridge: select the bridge to choose the Enterprise, NASA Shuttle, or astronaut as the traveler and edit the far-side nebula.

04

Choose how you observe

Camera gives you Orbit, Look 360°, and Free roam. In Free roam, drag to choose a heading and scroll or pinch to travel. Track or ride any physical target from the same menu. VR uses a compatible headset and WebXR browser. Every control stays available when the viewing panel is expanded.

Choose how you render. Adaptive selects the same Low, Medium, and High modes available in the menu. It steps down below 30 FPS and checks whether it can step up again. The current mode is shown beside the frame rate. Ultra is always manual: choose it for maximum detail, pause at a view you like, then use Save image. A slow Ultra frame is expected on less powerful GPUs. Picture renders a separate high-resolution still in small tiles, with progress, cancellation, and a downloadable result.

MouseDrag to orbit · wheel to zoom · middle-drag to look
TouchSelect Orbit, Look 360°, or Free roam · drag to steer · pinch to zoom or travel
KeyboardArrow keys to orbit · Shift + arrows to look · + / − to zoom · W / S to travel in Free roam

The Black hole math and Warp field math notebooks explain the equations, coordinate diagrams, and the limits of each visual model. Everything needed to run is included locally.
